summary: The note describes the handicap principle, a disputed hypothesis proposed by Israeli biologist Amotz Zahavi in 1975 to explain how costly sexual signals can be honest between animals with conflicting interests. It covers the theory's history, Alan Grafen's game-theory support and Thomas Getty's critique of its additive-cost assumption, cheap-talk counter-models, predictions and examples such as stotting and the Arabian babbler, and the immunocompetence handicap theory. The note concludes the principle remains unconfirmed empirically, and Penn and Számadó proposed in 2019 that it be abandoned.
one_line: Overview of the disputed handicap principle, Amotz Zahavi's 1975 theory that costly signals in sexual selection and animal communication are honest.
key_facts: The handicap principle was proposed in 1975 by the Israeli biologist Amotz Zahavi.
The handicap principle asserts that secondary sexual characteristics are costly signals that are reliable indicators of the signaller's quality.
The British biologist John Maynard Smith was a notable early critic of Zahavi's ideas.
Alan Grafen's signalling game model is described as essentially a rediscovery of the Canadian-American economist Michael Spence's job market signalling model.
The American biologist Thomas Getty showed in a series of papers that Grafen's proof depends on an additive cost-benefit assumption.
Dustin J. Penn and Szabolcs Számadó stated in 2019 that there was still no empirical evidence for evolutionary pressure for wasteful biology or acts, and proposed abandoning the handicap principle.
Models of signals without handicapping costs show that cheap talk may be an evolutionarily stable form of communication.
Zahavi invoked the gift-giving potlatch ceremony as a human example of the handicap principle, tracing the interpretation to Thorstein Veblen's concept of conspicuous consumption.
Jared Diamond proposed that certain risky human behaviours, such as bungee jumping, may be expressions of instincts evolved through the handicap principle.
Zahavi interpreted stotting in gazelles as each gazelle communicating that it was a fitter individual than its fellows.
Zahavi studied the Arabian babbler, whose helping-at-the-nest behaviour often occurs among unrelated individuals and cannot be explained by kin selection.
Patrice David showed that in the stalk-eyed fly Cyrtodiopsis dalmanni, genetic variation underlies how the male sexual ornament, eye span, responds to environmental stress.
Larks sing while being chased by merlins, telling their predator that they will be difficult to capture.
The immunocompetence handicap theory suggests androgen-mediated traits accurately signal condition due to the immunosuppressive effects of androgens.
A review of empirical studies of the immunocompetence handicap theory found weak support.
